description: Artemis_gh is a team of colleagues bringing together curiosity, creativity, and technical skills to tackle NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We're taking on The Earth Information Jukebox, exploring how Earth data can be transformed into an engaging musical and scientific experience. Our interests span software development, data analysis, Earth science, visualization, and creative design. We look forward to learning, experimenting, and building together.
summary: EarthSona is a web “Earth Jukebox” that turns NASA’s global temperature record into sound. Each year of the record becomes one note, and warmer years sound higher, while a bar chart fills in as the notes play. Instead of analysing animation frames, it sonifies the NASA GISTEMP numbers behind NASA’s global temperature visualization, so the sound and the picture tell the same story. It is built for blind and low-vision users and for anyone who learns by listening, with keyboard control, screen-reader announcements, a plain-language description of the trend, and a table of every value. It matters because a slow warming trend is easy to miss, and hearing it makes the change something you can feel.
details:
EarthSona plays NASA’s global temperature record as music. Pitch maps to temperature: the coolest year in the record is the lowest note and the warmest is the highest, across about two octaves. Time maps to the order of notes, one per year. Bars (red for warmer than the 1951–1980 average, blue for cooler) fill in as each note plays. Listeners can click the chart to jump to a year, choose a period, speed and instrument, and switch between a pentatonic scale and exact pitch.

Data: NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 annual global anomalies. When the page opens it requests NASA’s full table. If that fails, it uses a bundled NASA copy (2001–2025) and says which one is shown. Two clearly labelled sample tracks (rainfall and vegetation) use made-up numbers to show how other datasets could sound.

Impact: an audio companion to NASA’s temperature visualizations for blind and low-vision users, classrooms, and anyone who learns by listening. Accessibility features include keyboard control, screen-reader announcements, a plain-language summary and a table of all values.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG and the Web Audio API, with no servers or outside libraries. The demo deck was made with LaTeX Beamer.

Approach: we sonify the data behind the visualization rather than analysing image frames, which keeps the sound exact and traceable to NASA’s numbers. A scale option balances accuracy with musicality, and every data source is labelled honestly.
dataRefs: NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4)
NASA SVS: Global Temperature Anomalies from 1880 to 2025
projectRefs: Lenssen et al. 2024, GISTEMPv4 uncertainty ensemble (J. Geophys. Res. Atmos.)
LaTeX Beamer (presentation class used for the demo deck)
TikZ/PGF (used to draw the deck’s chart)
ChatGPT (OpenAI), used to draft the page code
